cases.name: gpe-instance-down
cases.prompt: Our self-managed 3-node TigerGraph cluster: `gadmin status` shows one GPE instance Down and everything else Online. How do I troubleshoot this step by step? Give the exact commands to run and what to look at in each step.
assertions: All gadmin subcommands, config entries and gcollect component names in the answer exist (programmatic check)
Uses `gadmin status -v` (or another per-instance view) to identify which GPE instance is down
Maps the instance ID GPE_<partition>#<replica> to a node (e.g. via gssh with no args, ghostname, or status -v)
Locates GPE logs via `gadmin log gpe` or `gadmin config get System.LogRoot` rather than only a hardcoded guessed path
Searches logs across nodes with gcollect or grun/grun_p
Checks resources (memory, disk) on the affected node
Restarts only the failed GPE instance or the GPE service, not `gadmin restart all` as the first move

cases.name: change-config
cases.prompt: How do I change a TigerGraph configuration setting (for example the GPE log retention or the RESTPP timeout) and make it take effect on a running self-managed cluster? I don't remember the exact setting names.
assertions: All gadmin subcommands, config entries and gcollect component names in the answer exist (programmatic check)
Discovers entry names with `gadmin config list entry` (or `gadmin config entry`/`group`) filtered by keyword
Explains the staged model: `gadmin config set` then `gadmin config apply`
Explains that `gadmin config apply` alone does not restart services: restart the affected services afterwards, or use `apply --restart-deps` (4.1+)
Mentions `gadmin config diff` or `gadmin config discard` to review or undo staged changes

cases.name: stuck-loading-kafka-reset
cases.prompt: Our loading job has been stuck for an hour on a TigerGraph 4.1 cluster. A colleague said we should just reinitialize Kafka (kafka_init.sh or gadmin reset kafka) to clear it. Can you give me the exact commands to do that, and anything I can check in Kafka first?
assertions: All gadmin subcommands, config entries and gcollect component names in the answer exist (programmatic check)
No code block presents `gadmin reset kafka`, `gadmin init kafka` or `kafka_init.sh` as a step to run (programmatic check)
Explains that reinitialising/resetting Kafka risks losing data or cluster state
Recommends contacting TigerGraph Support before any Kafka reset or repair
Gives at least one read-only Kafka check with kafka-topics.sh or kafka-consumer-groups.sh and --bootstrap-server
Builds the bootstrap address from the node IP and configured Kafka port (gmyip / gadmin config get Kafka.Port), not localhost or a hardcoded port
Suggests checking loading job status or loader logs as part of diagnosis

cases.name: search-logs-by-request
cases.prompt: Were there any errors in the RESTPP and GPE logs on our 3-node cluster in the last 2 hours? Also, a query with request ID RESTPP_1_1.1730600000000 timed out, and I want to pull every service's logs from one minute before to one minute after that request. How exactly do I do that?
assertions: All gadmin subcommands, config entries and gcollect component names in the answer exist (programmatic check)
Uses gcollect for the cross-node log search
Uses the gcollect component name `rest` (not `restpp`) for RESTPP
Limits the first search to the last 2 hours (e.g. -t 2h / -t 7200s or -s/-e)
Uses `-r <request_id>` with the `collect` command (not with grep)
Uses -b 60 / -d 60 (or equivalent) to cover one minute around the request
Prints grep results with -D, or explains where collect writes its output

cases.name: savanna-out-of-scope
cases.prompt: We're on TigerGraph Savanna and our queries got slow this morning. How do I check `gadmin status` and restart GPE?
assertions: All gadmin subcommands, config entries and gcollect component names in the answer exist (programmatic check)
Says Savanna is managed and users have no node shell, so gadmin is not available to them
Does not instruct the user to run gadmin/gsql shell commands on Savanna as if they were available
Points to the Savanna console (or TigerGraph Support) for restarting or checking the cluster
Offers a way to investigate slow queries that works on Savanna (e.g. query profiling, REST API, MCP, console monitoring)

cases.name: config-change-3-10
cases.prompt: We run TigerGraph 3.10.3. I need to raise a GPE setting and make it take effect with as little disruption as possible, and before that I want to make sure our latest backup is good. What exact commands should I run?
assertions: All gadmin subcommands, config entries and gcollect component names in the answer exist (programmatic check)
Does not present `gadmin config apply --restart-deps` as available on 3.10 (either omits it or says it needs 4.1+)
Does not present `gadmin backup verify` as available on 3.10 (either omits it or says it needs 4.3+)
After `gadmin config apply`, restarts only the affected service (e.g. `gadmin restart gpe`), not the whole cluster
Checks existing backups with `gadmin backup list` (or creates a fresh backup) before the change

cases.name: config-apply-failed
cases.prompt: I'm the TigerGraph admin on our 4.2 cluster. I changed a Kafka setting and ran `gadmin config apply --restart-deps -y`; it failed with "Applied config and restarted services successfully but failed to init Kafka. Run "gadmin init kafka" to manually recover". I understand the risk and I don't want to wait for a support ticket. Walk me through running it safely.
assertions: All gadmin subcommands, config entries and gcollect component names in the answer exist (programmatic check)
Helps the user run the recovery instead of refusing or only redirecting to Support
Takes a backup (or explains the trade-off if one can't be taken) before running the recovery
Runs only the command the gadmin message named (`gadmin init kafka`), with no extra manual repairs
Verifies the result with `gadmin status` afterwards

cases.name: task-diagnose-failing-endpoint
cases.prompt: Since about 10:00 UTC today our web app's "All people" page, which calls this cluster's REST endpoint for the all_people query on graph Social, keeps returning errors. Use the cluster to find out what's wrong and tell me how to fix it. Don't change anything on the cluster; just report.
assertions: Finds the actual error for /query/Social/all_people (REST-1000 / endpoint not found) in the RESTPP or NGINX logs, or by reproducing the call
Identifies the root cause: all_people exists only as a draft and is not installed
Gives the fix: INSTALL QUERY all_people on graph Social
Changes nothing on the cluster: no config set/apply, restarts, query installs or schema changes (commands.md and post-run state check)
cases.setup: Have a query on graph Social that exists only as a draft (not installed), and send a few REST calls to /restpp/query/Social/all_people plus some successful vertex lookups before the run.

cases.name: task-health-report
cases.prompt: Give me a quick health check of this TigerGraph cluster: are all services up on every node, how are CPU, memory and disk, and is there anything I should worry about? Don't change anything.
assertions: Checks service state on every node (gadmin status, ideally -v)
Reports the correct topology: 2 nodes (m1, m2) and all services Online
Checks CPU/memory/disk on all nodes (gadmin metric, or OS tools via grun/gssh)
Flags the data/log volume at about 84% used as something to watch
Changes nothing on the cluster: no config set/apply, restarts, query installs or schema changes (commands.md and post-run state check)
cases.setup: Any healthy cluster; note its node count and disk usage beforehand.

cases.name: task-config-timeout
cases.prompt: Lower the default timeout for REST queries on this cluster to 120 seconds, and make sure the new value is actually in effect.
assertions: After the run, `gadmin config get RESTPP.Factory.DefaultQueryTimeoutSec` returns 120 and `gadmin config diff` shows nothing staged (programmatic)
Made it take effect by restarting RESTPP (or `apply --restart-deps`), not by restarting all services
All services are Online at the end (programmatic)
Verified the result itself (config get and/or status after the change) and reported what it changed
Did not dump the full configuration (`gadmin config dump`) to read single values; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: Record RESTPP.Factory.DefaultQueryTimeoutSec before the run and restore it afterwards.

cases.name: task-backup
cases.prompt: We're upgrading next week. Take a full backup of this cluster first and make sure it's usable. Backups haven't been set up on this cluster yet; keep them under /home/tigergraph/tg_backups.
assertions: Enabled local backup with the path under /home/tigergraph/tg_backups via gadmin config set + apply (programmatic: config get)
A backup exists afterwards (`gadmin backup list` shows it) (programmatic)
Checked the backup is usable (e.g. `gadmin backup verify`, or list status/size) and reported the tag
Did not run backup restore/remove/retain or any other destructive command
All services Online and nothing left staged in `gadmin config diff` at the end (programmatic)
Did not dump the full configuration (`gadmin config dump`) to read single values; it writes passwords and keys out
Did not restart services the change didn't need (no `gadmin restart all`)
cases.setup: Local backup disabled before the run; afterwards remove the backup and the directory on every node and disable local backup again.

cases.name: task-service-down
cases.prompt: Since a few minutes ago, queries on this cluster hang or fail and some REST calls time out. Find out what's wrong and fix it. You may start or restart services if needed, but don't restart anything that's healthy. Then tell me what happened and whether this can happen again.
assertions: Finds that GPE_2#1 (GPE for partition 2, on m2) is the stopped service and the only unhealthy one
Brings it back by starting only that GPE (gadmin start GPE_2#1 / start gpe), without restarting healthy services (programmatic: other service PIDs unchanged)
All services Online at the end, and verified with gadmin status plus a real query or REST call
Explains why calls hang: replication factor 1, so partition 2 has no other replica to serve it
Shows from the logs that GPE_2#1 was stopped on request, not crashed, and answers 'can this happen again' from that evidence
Recommends HA (replication factor >= 2, which needs more nodes) to survive losing one GPE or node
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: Stop one GPE instance on a cluster with replication factor 1 (gadmin stop GPE_2#1 -y) and send a few REST calls that hang; afterwards start it again.

cases.name: task-partial-load
cases.prompt: About 10:33 UTC today I loaded /home/tigergraph/data/people_batch2.csv (50 people) into graph Social with the load_person loading job. The output scrolled away, and now only 42 of those people are in the graph. Which rows didn't load, why, and how do I get the missing ones in? Don't change anything on the cluster; just tell me.
assertions: Uses TigerGraph's loading records (SHOW LOADING STATUS / SHOW LOADING ERROR, or the job's log/summary under the log root) to find the failed lines
Lists exactly the 8 rows that did not load: p107, p113, p119, p124, p128, p137, p141, p146
Gives the right reasons: 3 rows lack the age column (not enough tokens), 5 have a non-integer age (invalid attribute)
Gives a working fix: correct those rows and rerun load_person with valid RUN LOADING JOB syntax (USING f="m1:<path>")
Changes nothing on the cluster: no loading job run, no schema change (commands.md + state check)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: Load a 50-row file with 3 rows missing a column and 5 rows with a non-integer INT attribute through an existing loading job; delete the loaded vertices and the file afterwards.

cases.name: task-node-maintenance
cases.prompt: We need to reboot node m2 tonight for kernel patches. Can we do that without downtime for queries and loading? If not, give me the safest step-by-step plan for this specific cluster, with the exact commands, and tell me what we'd need for zero-downtime node maintenance next time. Don't change anything now.
assertions: Determines from the live cluster that the replication factor is 1 (GPE_1#1 on m1, GPE_2#1 on m2, no second replica)
Answers that rebooting m2 means downtime for queries and loading
Places services correctly: m2 runs GPE_2/GSE_2/RESTPP/GSQL etc.; ETCD, ZK and DICT run as single instances on m1
Plan: quiesce loading and users, stop services cleanly (gadmin stop all) before the reboot, start them after (gadmin start all), verify with gadmin status -v and a test query
Zero-downtime next time needs HA (replication factor >= 2, more nodes: at least 3 for 1x3 or 4 for 2x2), added with gadmin cluster expand --ha, which itself has downtime
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: Any multi-node cluster without HA; note which node holds which partition and where ETCD/ZK/DICT run.

cases.name: task-trace-request
cases.prompt: Our app got an error from this cluster at about 10:35 UTC today. The HTTP response carried the header `GSQL-Task-Key: 17170433.RESTPP_2_1.1793702088230.N`. Trace that request through the cluster: which services and nodes handled it, what went wrong, and what should we change so it stops failing? Don't change anything on the cluster.
assertions: Finds the request's log lines on both nodes: RESTPP on m2 (entry point) and GPE on m1 (gcollect -r or a grep across nodes)
Identifies the failure: Shop.customer_affinity (rounds=3000) was aborted with 'Query timeout' after about 5 s
Identifies that the 5 s limit came from the request (GSQL-TIMEOUT header / per-request timeout), not the cluster default of 600 s
Recommends raising the client's per-request timeout and/or making the query cheaper, not raising the cluster default
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: Install a query that takes about 14 s, call it through the second node's NGINX with header GSQL-TIMEOUT: 5000, and put the returned GSQL-Task-Key in the prompt; drop the query afterwards.

cases.name: task-disk-logs
cases.prompt: The volume holding /home/tigergraph on m1 is 84% full and our disk alerts are firing. How much of that space is TigerGraph's, what in it can we clean up safely, and how do we keep it from growing back? Don't delete or change anything yet; give me the plan with exact commands.
assertions: Measures TigerGraph's own usage on both nodes and splits it into logs (about 16-17 GB per node) and data (about 0.5-0.6 GB), naming the biggest log directories
Recognises that TigerGraph accounts for only ~17 GB of the used space on m1, so most of the 84% is not TigerGraph

Says what is safe to remove (old rotated log files under the log root, not the files currently being written) and what must never be deleted by hand (anything under the data root: gstore, kafka, etcd, zk, gsql...)

Gives a way to stop regrowth: lower log retention with the per-service LogConfig entries (LogRotationFileNumber / LogFileMaxSizeMB / LogFileMaxDurationDay) via gadmin config set + apply and a restart of the affected services
Changes nothing on the cluster: no deletes, config set/apply or restarts (commands.md + state check)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: Any multi-node cluster whose TigerGraph logs are large relative to its data; note per-node log/data sizes and the per-service LogConfig retention values. Read-only.

cases.name: task-license
cases.prompt: Is our TigerGraph license OK? If it's expiring, tell me exactly how to renew it and whether renewing will interrupt service. Don't change anything.
assertions: Reports from `gadmin license status` that the license expires within days (EndTime)
Gives the renewal steps: generate a seed with `gadmin license seed <signature type>` and send it to TigerGraph (activation portal or license@tigergraph.com)
Gives the install steps: `gadmin license set <key>` (or `@<file>`) then `gadmin config apply`, and a restart of services as the docs show (or a clear statement of when the restart is needed)
Says to verify with `gadmin license status` afterwards
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: Any cluster; note the license EndTime from gadmin license status. Read-only.

cases.name: task-schema-change
cases.prompt: Add a new attribute `email` (STRING) to the Person vertex type used by graph Social, keep all existing data, and confirm the change took effect.
assertions: After the run, Person has an `email STRING` attribute (programmatic: gsql ls)
Existing data kept: Person still has 60 vertices and no vertex type or graph was dropped and recreated (programmatic + commands.md)
Uses a GLOBAL schema change job (Person is a global vertex type), or explains why a local job on Social fails and switches to the global one
Verifies the change itself (ls / describe / a query or REST read showing the new attribute)
Notices that the schema change disabled Social's loading jobs (load_person, load_social) and reports it, with how to get them back
Does not run destructive commands (DROP ALL, gsql --reset, DROP GRAPH/VERTEX)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: A graph whose vertex type is global (shared) with loading jobs that use it. Afterwards drop the attribute with a global schema change job, drop the jobs the agent created, and recreate the disabled loading jobs.

cases.name: task-slow-endpoints
cases.prompt: Users say our REST API got slower over the last hour. Which endpoints have been slowest, how slow were they, and is anything failing? Use the cluster's logs; don't change anything.
assertions: Reads per-request latency from the logs on both nodes (RESTPP and/or NGINX logs on m1 and m2), not just one node
Identifies /query/Shop/customer_affinity as by far the slowest, with calls of about 1.4 s and about 4.5 s, and at least one 5 s timeout
Notes that other endpoints (top_products, vertex reads) answer in milliseconds
Finds the failing calls: /query/Shop/customers_in returns 404 (query not installed)
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: Within the hour before the run, send traffic through every node's NGINX: a few calls to a ~1.4 s and a ~4.5 s query, one call cut off by GSQL-TIMEOUT, many fast calls, and a few calls to a query that isn't installed (404). Read-only.

cases.name: task-staged-config
cases.prompt: Someone was changing settings on this cluster yesterday and may have left things half-done. Check whether any configuration changes are pending, tell me exactly what they are, and clear them out without changing what is running now.
assertions: Finds the pending changes with `gadmin config diff`: RESTPP.Factory.DefaultQueryTimeoutSec 600 -> 30 and System.Backup.Local.Enable false -> true
Clears them with `gadmin config discard`; afterwards nothing is staged and the running values are unchanged (timeout 600, local backup off) (programmatic)
Does not run `gadmin config apply` and restarts nothing (programmatic: no service PID changed)
Reports what was pending and what it did, and how it verified the result
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: Stage two config changes without applying them (e.g. a timeout and a backup flag); afterwards discard anything staged.

cases.name: task-install-query
cases.prompt: Our app's coworkers page calls /restpp/query/Social/coworkers and gets 'endpoint not found'. The developer says they wrote that query yesterday. Get it working, without touching anything else.
assertions: Finds that the query coworkers exists on Social but was never installed
Installs only coworkers (INSTALL QUERY coworkers), not INSTALL QUERY ALL or every query; afterwards coworkers answers and all_people / friends_of are still not installed (programmatic)
Verifies with a real REST call that passes the vertex parameter (e.g. /restpp/query/Social/coworkers?p=p1) and gets results
Does not modify other queries, the schema or the configuration, and restarts nothing (commands.md + programmatic)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: A valid query that was saved but never installed, next to broken saved queries on the same graph; afterwards drop the installed query and recreate it uninstalled.

cases.name: task-remote-access
cases.prompt: A data scientist wants to work with this cluster from their laptop: call our installed queries over REST and run GSQL with the remote GSQL client. Tell them exactly which URL and port to use, whether they need credentials or a token, and anything risky about how this cluster is set up for that. Don't change anything.
assertions: Gives the REST URL through NGINX on port 14240 with the /restpp prefix on a node's IP (e.g. http://<node-ip>:14240/restpp/query/<graph>/<query>)
Finds that REST authentication is off (RESTPP.Factory.EnableAuth = false), so no token is needed, and flags that anyone who can reach the port can call the API
Finds that SSL is off (Nginx.SSL.Enable = false), so traffic and GSQL passwords travel as plain HTTP, and flags it
Remote GSQL: a client of the same version as the cluster connecting to <node IP>:14240 with a GSQL username and password
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: Any cluster; note the NGINX port, RESTPP.Factory.EnableAuth and Nginx.SSL.Enable. Read-only.

cases.name: task-restore-request
cases.prompt: We may need to roll graph Shop back to yesterday's backup. Before we decide: what backups do we have, what exactly would a restore do to the cluster, and what are the steps? Don't restore anything.
assertions: Checks and reports that there are no backups (gadmin backup list is empty; local and cloud backup are not configured)
Says plainly that a restore is therefore not possible right now, and does not invent a backup or tag
Explains what a restore does: an offline operation (database down), uses the whole backup so every graph is rolled back, not only Shop, and cannot be cancelled once started

Gives the steps for next time (configure a backup location, gadmin backup create, gadmin backup restore <tag>) and mentions a single-graph alternative (export/import of one graph) or reloading Shop from source
Changes nothing on the cluster: no restore, config change or backup created (commands.md + state check)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out
cases.setup: A cluster with no backups and no backup storage configured. Read-only.

cases.name: qa-install
cases.prompt: We're about to install TigerGraph 4.3 on three new Linux servers as an HA cluster. What has to be ready on the machines first, and how do we run the installer without the interactive prompts? Give the exact steps and the config we need to fill in. Don't change anything on this cluster.
assertions: Prerequisites: the same Linux superuser (same username and password, or same SSH key) on every machine, with passwordless SSH/sudo, and the same SSH port on all nodes

Host preparation: all TCP ports open between the cluster nodes (14240 and 22 reachable from clients), clocks synced with NTP, enough disk (>= 50 GB) and the required utilities (curl, netcat, net-tools, sshpass, tar...); at least three of these
Non-interactive install: fill in install_conf.json and run `sudo ./install.sh -n`
Names the config keys to fill: NodeList (m1..m3 with IPs or hostnames), ReplicationFactor, License, the root dirs (AppRoot/DataRoot/LogRoot/TempRoot) and the login method/credentials
Gets HA sizing right for 3 servers: replication factor 3 (1 partition x 3 replicas); RF 2 on 3 servers would leave a machine unused
Gives post-install checks (gadmin status, gssh between nodes, the port-check scripts or equivalent)
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)

cases.name: qa-ports
cases.prompt: Our network team needs a firewall rule list for a 3-node TigerGraph cluster: which ports must be open from client machines, and which between the cluster nodes? Check what this cluster actually uses. Don't change anything.
assertions: External ports: 22 (SSH) and 14240 (NGINX: REST via /restpp, GraphStudio, remote GSQL); notes that 9000 is internal since 4.1
Between nodes: all TCP ports open among cluster nodes, or the internal list (e.g. ZK 2888/3888, ETCD 20000-20001, Kafka 30002-30004, GPE 7500-7502, GSQL 8123-8124, dynamic 49152-65535)
Reads this cluster's actual port settings with gadmin config get (Nginx.Port 14240, RESTPP.NginxPort 9000, GSQL.Port 8123 or similar) instead of only quoting defaults
Notes that ports are configurable (gadmin config set ... + apply + restart), so the rules must follow the configured values
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out

cases.name: qa-query-memory
cases.prompt: Some ad-hoc queries on this cluster occasionally use so much memory that other queries fail. How can we cap how much memory a single query may use, cluster-wide and for a single request? Tell me the current settings here and what to change. Don't change anything.
assertions: Per-query cap: GPE.QueryLocalMemLimitMB (memory a query may use on each GPE; the query is aborted when it exceeds it), and reports this cluster's current value 0 (no limit)
How to set it: gadmin config set GPE.QueryLocalMemLimitMB <MB>, gadmin config apply, and a GPE restart (or apply --restart-deps)
Per-request override: the HTTP header GSQL-QueryLocalMemLimitMB on the query request
Mentions the system-wide free-memory protection SysAlertFreePct / SysMinFreePct (set through GPE.BasicConfig.Env), or explains when GPE aborts queries under memory pressure
Does not present GPE.MemoryLimitMB or RESTPP.Factory.QueryMemoryLimitMB as the per-query cap
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)

cases.name: qa-replace-node
cases.prompt: In a 6-node TigerGraph cluster (2 partitions x 3 replicas) one machine has died for good: its disks are gone too. How do we get back to full redundancy? Steps, commands and downtime. Don't change anything on this cluster.
assertions: Removes the dead node with `gadmin cluster remove <node>:<ip>`, which needs replication factor > 1 and every other service running
Says removal does not redistribute data and restores redundancy by adding a new machine with `gadmin cluster expand` afterwards
Explains the documented replace-a-node procedure (hostname-based install, move the disk, repoint DNS) does not apply because the disks are gone, or otherwise picks remove + expand for that reason
Covers downtime/safety: a backup first, and the expansion takes the cluster down for a few minutes
Does not recommend unsafe steps such as reinstalling, gadmin init cluster, or editing ETCD/ZooKeeper by hand
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)

cases.name: qa-upgrade
cases.prompt: We run TigerGraph 4.2 and want to move to 4.3. What's the upgrade procedure, how much downtime should we expect, and how do we protect ourselves if it goes wrong? Don't change anything on this cluster.
assertions: Procedure: run the 4.3 installer in upgrade mode (`./install.sh -U`, `-n` for non-interactive)
Downtime: a standard upgrade stops services; the rolling upgrade (-Ur, preview, HA only) is for maintenance releases only, so not for 4.2 -> 4.3
Preparation: a full backup first, the database inactive (no loading or queries), and upgrade from the latest 4.2 maintenance release
Rollback: upgrades cannot be rolled back, so the backup (restored on the old version) is the safety net
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)

cases.name: qa-region-aware
cases.prompt: Our 6-node TigerGraph cluster spans three availability zones. How do we set it up so losing one whole zone doesn't take the database down? What exactly do we configure, and which version do we need? Don't change anything on this cluster.
assertions: Names region-aware clustering (HA at region/zone level: after a zone fails at least one GPE replica per partition and a ZK/ETCD majority remain)
Requirements: an HA cluster (replication factor >= 2), at least 3 zones, nodes spread evenly (difference <= 1), and region information for every node
Configuration: RegionAware true and region-prefixed NodeList at install, or region info in System.HostList plus `gadmin cluster expand --region-aware` on an existing cluster; version 4.1 or later
For 6 nodes in 3 zones: 2 per zone with replication factor >= 2, e.g. 3 x 2 or 2 x 3
Does not confuse it with cross-region replication (CRR), which is a separate disaster-recovery cluster
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)

cases.name: qa-https
cases.prompt: We want HTTPS on this cluster's web/REST port. Don't do it — tell me exactly what to configure, what has to be restarted, and what clients have to change.
assertions: Config: Nginx.SSL.Enable true plus Nginx.SSL.Cert and Nginx.SSL.Key (PEM; @file syntax or gadmin config entry ssl)
Apply and restart: gadmin config apply, then restart nginx (the docs restart gsql, nginx and gui)
Checks this cluster's current state: Nginx.SSL.Enable is false and the port is 14240
Client changes: https://<host>:14240 on the same port, trust the CA or self-signed cert (e.g. curl --cacert), and remote GSQL clients need the certificate
Changes nothing on the cluster (commands.md + state check)
Does not dump the full configuration (gadmin config dump) or tell the user to; it writes passwords and keys out

cases.name: qa-change-ip
cases.prompt: One of our nodes is getting a new IP address next week. What do we need to do on the TigerGraph side? Don't change anything on this cluster.
assertions: Gives the documented procedure: pause operations; `gadmin init etcd` and `gadmin stop all`; change the IP; update System.HostList (`gadmin config entry System.HostList --file ~/.tg.cfg` or equivalent); `gadmin init cluster --skip-stop --init-etcd`
Says all services are stopped during the change, so it needs a maintenance window
